name: EcoBoard: Pressed Oyster Mycelia Panel Development
description: Research and development into optimizing substrate mixtures and pressing techniques for producing durable, fire-resistant construction boards from *Pleurotus ostreatus* (Oyster Mushroom) mycelium.
goal: Finalize a low-cost, scalable production method that yields a panel with an R-value above 2.5 and compressive strength exceeding 50 PSI.
notes: Current tests show good insulation properties, but edge bonding requires further refinement. Focusing next on developing the concrete mycelia glue for this application.

name: Bio-Cube Edible Substrates and Shelf-Life Trials
description: A food science trial focused on enriching spent mushroom substrate (SMS) with nutrients to create edible, compact bio-cubes for human consumption. Includes taste tests, nutritional analysis, and shelf-life studies.
goal: Achieve a minimum 14-day refrigerated shelf life and ensure palatable taste and texture, demonstrating proof-of-concept for nutrient-dense edible mycelium products.
notes: Collaboration secured with the local university's food safety lab. Initial nutrient calculations are complete, pending final recipe development ('recipes' collection will contain the mix formulas).

name: MycoBinder: Development of Bio-Cementation Mycelia Glue
description: Experimentation with various fungal strains and liquid culture media to produce a strong, waterproof, and structural mycelia-based glue compatible with concrete and construction aggregates.
goal: Develop a biological adhesive with sheer strength exceeding 200 PSI for non-load-bearing applications, replacing 30% of Portland cement in small batches.
notes: Ganoderma strain shows best adhesion properties under high humidity, but the cure time is too long (4 days). Need to trial Elixir server-based automated environmental controls for cure optimization.

name: Community Resilience & Accessible Fungi Cultivation Trial (CRAFT)
description: A field trial focused on the deployment of simple, low-tech, and decentralized fungi cultivation kits in underserved communities to enhance local food security and provide educational tooling.
goal: Successfully deploy 100 cultivation kits and measure the resulting yield and community engagement over a six-month period. Develop educational content (vanilla JS/static serving) for transparency.
notes: Trial successful. Data gathered is now being prepared for the public-facing 'biodiversity token transparency' dashboard built with vanilla JS and static serving. Focus is now on the tokenization layer.
